how: Fill each item's `record` with one of {"new": {...}}, {"table": "...", "id": n} or {"reason": "..."}, then Reading.ps1 -Step Record -Label m64-dedicate -File <this file>. New open items go in `new_items` (the Open-Item.ps1 -Action Add shape, D-b).

hit_unread.guide: A strand hit with no face and no reason. Give the hit its face (and the observation it goes into), or the reason it has none.

meaning_missing.guide: A word in scope with no meaning senses (or, for Greek, no Mounce entry). Pull it through the spine route and name the row, or give the reason it is not needed for this reading.

not_read.guide: A verse with no observation and no strand face. Read it in its passage; record what it states about the inner being (a new observation), name an existing observation that already covers it, or give the reason it holds nothing.

open_item.guide: An open item that matches the scope: read for what it asks, and record what the reading found (an observation, or a response of kind touched). It is not closed here: closing is decided in synergy (gate 2).

new.text: Among the vowed gifts, a person dedicates what is his own: "When a man dedicates his house as a holy gift to the Lord, the priest shall value it as either good or bad" (Lev 27:14); part of his land, "the valuation shall be in proportion to its seed" (27:16), from or after the jubilee (27:17-18); a field he has bought (27:22). The gift can be taken back at a cost: "if the donor wishes to redeem his house, he shall add a fifth" (27:15; 27:19). If it is not redeemed, "it shall not be redeemed anymore" (27:20).
new.meaning: Dedicating is a person giving what is his own to the Lord, and the gift is measured by another, can be bought back at a cost, and can be lost for good.
new.setting: Leviticus 27, the law of vowed gifts. The ESV's "wishes" renders the redeem verb with "if" (H1350A, H0518A); no will word stands in the Hebrew.
new.implication: The giver's act is real, and the law sets its worth and its limits, not the giver.
new.parties: the giver; the priest; the Lord

items.text: “ But a firstborn of animals, which as a firstborn belongs to the Lord, no man may dedicate; whether ox or sheep, it is the Lord’s.
file_lines: _analytics/Clusters/M64 - will-resolve/m64-H6942H-verses-v1-20261006.md:80 | Lev 27:26 | "dedicate" HVhi3ms | M37 firstborn "firstborn"; M37 to be/bear firstborn "firstborn" | “ But a firstborn of animals, which as a firstborn belongs to the Lord, no man may dedicate; whether ox or sheep, it is the Lord’s. |

new.text: What is already the Lord's cannot be given as one's own: "a firstborn of animals, which as a firstborn belongs to the Lord, no man may dedicate; whether ox or sheep, it is the Lord's" (Lev 27:26). Where it is commanded, the dedication is set beside a remembered redemption: "Consecrate to me all the firstborn ... is mine" (Exo 13:2), then "Remember this day in which you came out from Egypt" (13:3); "All the firstborn males ... you shall dedicate to the Lord your God" (Deu 15:19), after "you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God redeemed you" (15:15).
new.meaning: The giving has a limit: what belongs to the Lord is not the giver's to offer, and the commanded dedication answers a redemption remembered.
new.implication: The firstborn is given back because it is already his, not offered from the giver's store.
new.parties: the Lord; Israel; the owner of the firstborn

new.text: The same giving can be turned to an idol. Micah's mother: "I dedicate the silver to the Lord from my hand for my son, to make a carved image and a metal image" (Judg 17:3), in days when "Everyone did what was right in his own eyes" (17:6). Israel "came to Baal-peor and consecrated themselves to the thing of shame, and became detestable like the thing they loved" (Hos 9:10), after "Like grapes in the wilderness, I found Israel". And one "who separates himself from me, taking his idols into his heart" (Eze 14:7), whose heart God means to "lay hold of" (14:5).
new.meaning: Giving oneself or one's goods can go to an idol in the Lord's name; a person becomes like what he gives himself to and loves, and separating from God is done with idols taken into the heart.
new.setting: Judges 17 (Micah's shrine); Hosea 9 (Baal-peor); Ezekiel 14 (the elders with idols in their hearts).
new.implication: What is loved shapes the one who gives himself to it (Hos 9:10).
new.parties: Micah and his mother; Israel at Baal-peor; the house of Israel and the sojourner; God

new.text: "Behold, I am about to build a house for the name of the Lord my God and dedicate it to him" (2Ch 2:4), after "Solomon purposed to build a temple" (2:1), and with "But who is able to build him a house, since heaven, even highest heaven, cannot contain him? Who am I to build a house for him, except as a place to make offerings before him?" (2:6).
new.meaning: The house is dedicated inside a purpose, and the one who dedicates it asks who he is to do it.
new.implication: The dedication is held with a humbling question.

items.text: And the people of Israel and Judah who lived in the cities of Judah also brought in the tithe of cattle and sheep, and the tithe of the dedicated things that had been dedicated to the Lord their God, and laid them in heaps.
file_lines: _analytics/Clusters/M64 - will-resolve/m64-H6942H-verses-v1-20261006.md:91 | 2Ch 31:6 | "dedicated" HVPsmpa | M61 holiness "dedicated things" | And the people of Israel and Judah who lived in the cities of Judah also brought in the tithe of cattle and sheep, and the tithe of the dedicated things that had been dedicated to the Lord their God, and laid them in heaps. |

new.text: Giving in abundance and with joy: "the people of Israel gave in abundance" (2Ch 31:5) and brought "the tithe of the dedicated things that had been dedicated to the Lord their God" (31:6), and when Hezekiah "saw the heaps, they blessed the Lord and his people Israel" (31:8). In Nehemiah "they set apart that which was for the Levites" (Neh 12:47), where "God had made them rejoice with great joy" (12:43).
new.meaning: The setting apart of gifts is done in abundance and joy, and is answered with blessing.
new.setting: 2 Chronicles 31 (Hezekiah); Nehemiah 12 (the dedication of the wall).
new.implication: Joy in the giving is named beside the act.
new.parties: the people; Hezekiah and the princes; the Levites and priests

items.text: “ Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.”
file_lines: _analytics/Clusters/M64 - will-resolve/m64-H6942H-verses-v1-20261006.md:93 | Jer 1:5 | "consecrated" HVhp1cs | M15 to know "knew"; M43 prophet "prophet" | “ Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.” |

new.text: "Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations" (Jer 1:5). Jeremiah answers, "Ah, Lord God! Behold, I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth" (1:6), and is told, "Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you" (1:8).
new.meaning: God's dedicating of a person comes before the person knows or wills; the person's answer is a shrinking that God meets with a sending and a presence.
new.setting: Jeremiah 1, the call; route A and B.
new.implication: The dedication is God's act, and the will that answers it is the person's.

new.text: "Should I weep and abstain in the fifth month, as I have done for so many years?" (Zec 7:3). God answers with the aim: "When you fasted and mourned in the fifth month and in the seventh, for these seventy years, was it for me that you fasted?" (7:5), "do you not eat for yourselves and drink for yourselves?" (7:6).
new.meaning: Abstaining is judged by whom it was for, not by its long keeping.
new.implication: A practice held for years can be asked what it was for.
new.parties: the people of Bethel; the priests and prophets; the Lord
